findings.description: The hardened review diff leaves out `--text`. The session can mark its files `-diff` (or `binary`) and the reviewer then sees only "Binary files differ" instead of the real code.
findings.body:
[`SECURITY_REVIEW_DIFF`](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/c2c908eb0bb054a880d03f05986b9dc45bacda1f/src/core/profile-compiler.service.ts#L568-L574) turns off diff drivers, textconv, the pager and colour, but it does not override the binary attribute. pup's own gate diff does. [`DIFF_SAFE_FLAGS`](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/c2c908eb0bb054a880d03f05986b9dc45bacda1f/src/core/git-diff.client.ts#L95-L100) adds `--text` for exactly this case: "a `* -diff` attribute or `diff.<driver>.binary` that turns every file into 'Binary files differ'" (decision 53).

The command runs with `-C .worktrees/<session-id>`, so git reads attributes from the session's own worktree. A session can hide every hunk in any of these ways:
- a `.gitattributes` with `* -diff` in its worktree, committed or not;
- a line in the shared `info/attributes`;
- `core.attributesFile`, `diff.<driver>.binary` or a small `core.bigFileThreshold` in the shared config.

`assertNoArmedGitDrivers` only runs inside the merge gate, after this review. Decision 53 also records that `core.attributesFile` and `core.bigFileThreshold` are outside what it refuses. When this happens, the xhigh subagent gets file names and no code, and the conductor reports a clean review of the very changes this step exists to inspect.

Fix: add `--text` to the final element (`--no-pager diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-color --text …`). Consider `--ignore-submodules=none` as well, since `diff.ignoreSubmodules=all` hides gitlink changes the same way. Update the pinned string at `src/core/profile-compiler.test.ts:950`.

findings.description: The session can steer `main` and `HEAD` in `main...HEAD`, so the reviewer can be shown an empty or decoy diff instead of what `pup merge --pr` pushes.
findings.body:
[`SECURITY_REVIEW_DIFF`](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/c2c908eb0bb054a880d03f05986b9dc45bacda1f/src/core/profile-compiler.service.ts#L568-L574) names both ends of the diff by bare name, inside the session's own worktree. The session controls both:
- **`main`:** a bare name resolves `refs/tags/main` before `refs/heads/main`. Tags live in the shared `$GIT_COMMON_DIR`, so `git tag main HEAD` makes the merge base equal HEAD, and the reviewer sees an empty diff. Git only prints an "ambiguous" warning on stderr.
- **`HEAD`:** this is the worktree's HEAD, and the session can detach it onto a harmless commit. `pup merge --pr` never reads that HEAD: it pins and pushes `refs/heads/pup/<session-id>` ([`merge-gate.service.ts:859`](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/c2c908eb0bb054a880d03f05986b9dc45bacda1f/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L855-L888)). The gate itself already handles "a session that detached it or switched branch".

Decision 80 settled this for every other review path: "a bare name resolves a same-named tag first, and the review must show what the gate merges." `review.service.ts:61-67`, `overlap.service.ts:52-56` and `conductor.service.ts:86-96` all name `refs/heads/<target>` and `refs/heads/<branch>`. This PR introduced the bare form, and this round rewrote the line as the trusted command without fixing it.

Fix: diff `refs/heads/<target>...refs/heads/pup/<session-id>`. The target is the main checkout's current branch (`merge-gate.service.ts:300`), not always `main`, so either the prompt should name it or the `main` assumption should be stated. Update the pinned string at `src/core/profile-compiler.test.ts:950`.

findings.description: The prompt cites "(decision 41)" for the session arming the shared git config's diff drivers and promisor remotes, but decision 41 is about refusing a launch whose scope collides with a live session; cite decision 83 (promisor/protocol pins) or 50 (drivers), or drop the parenthetical.

Now that a conductor-named `--model` no longer lifts the top-rung refusal, the `TopRungReachedError` text the conductor receives from `pup launch` still advises "relaunch it with an explicit `--model` and `--effort`", which the conductor will be refused again for; the message should hand the case to the operator.

Seven transports are pinned by name but `protocol.allow` itself is not, so a planted `protocol.allow=always` would still enable ftp/ftps or a `git-remote-<x>` helper for a lazy fetch if `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH` were ignored; pinning `-c protocol.allow=never` alongside costs nothing.

`SECURITY_REVIEW_DIFF` hand-copies the seven-transport list `NO_TRANSPORT` already holds in `dashboard.service.ts:468` (and the `core.fsmonitor`/`core.hooksPath` pins from `GIT_SAFE_CONFIG`), so a transport added in one place won't reach the other; it also sits in the service file rather than a `*.constants.ts` with JSDoc, unlike its sibling `SECURITY_REVIEW_EFFORT` (general.md §hardcoded values).

`launchTask` derives `operatorDecides` as `req.overrideVia !== 'conductor'`, so any programmatic caller that omits `overrideVia` gets the top-rung-lifting behaviour by default, the unsafe direction; defaulting to not lifting, or requiring `overrideVia` whenever `model`/`effort` is set, would make the trust explicit.

The newest-respawn timestamp lookup repeats the `events.map(...).lastIndexOf(...)` + `Date.parse(toIsoUtc(rows[i]?.created_at ?? ''))` idiom of the killed-event lookup a few lines above in the same function, and the two differ on an unparseable date (`|| 0` here, not there); one local helper would keep them in step.
The edited `nextWindowRoute` JSDoc line ("…but never that decision. A task re-tiered since its last window") runs past the file's wrap width; reflow the paragraph.
